summary: The climate has shifted, but farm plans haven’t: DalaShift turns 35 years of NASA climate data and current NASA satellite observations into a simple 5-year crop rotation plan for any irrigated field, piloted in Uzbekistan, in Uzbek, with income in so’m and water measured against what the farm actually gets.
details:
What it does: The climate has shifted, but farm plans haven’t. DalaShift is a free web app that gives any irrigated field a simple 5-year crop rotation plan. A farmer picks a field (or uses their phone’s location), sets how much irrigation water they get, and picks a goal: most income, balanced, or least water. DalaShift shows what to plant each year, a cautious income estimate in so’m, and water use against the farm’s own supply, compared with the usual wheat-cotton rotation, plus a plain-language “why”. It is Uzbek-first, with an English toggle and a detailed tab for experts.
How it works: NASA POWER daily weather (1991-2026) feeds an FAO-56 crop-water and climate-fit engine (sowing windows, frost, heat stress at flowering, irrigation need). A planner checks every possible 5-year sequence (up to 248,832 per farm) against rotation rules (no repeated cotton, legumes to restore soil, double cropping) and the water budget, then ranks them using FAOSTAT and local market prices. NASA SMAP soil moisture and HLS (Landsat + Sentinel-2) greenness show how dry and green the field is and confirm the crop calendars. 244 automated tests check the rules and numbers.
Benefits and impact: Replaying 2021-2025 at a Karshi field with real NASA weather, the usual wheat-cotton rotation ran short of water in 2 of 5 years. DalaShift’s balanced plan fit the water every year, used about 51% less water and earned about 20% more (estimate), with 2 legume years. The goal is less wasted water, healthier rotations and more stable farm income, explained in the farmer’s language on a phone.
Tools: Python (pandas, NumPy), Streamlit, a static web app (HTML/CSS/JavaScript, Leaflet, OpenStreetMap), reveal.js, pytest, NASA AppEEARS, Netlify, GitHub, and a Telegram bot (@dalashiftbot).
Creativity and factors considered: It plans five years ahead, not one season, and shows the trade-offs between income, water and soil. It uses Uzbek and so’m, and only suggests crops local markets buy. Numbers are cautious and assumptions are labelled. It handles real constraints like water limits and compulsory cotton/wheat. NASA POWER, SMAP and HLS are global, so a new region only needs its crop list and local prices. Uzbekistan is our pilot.
